title: Homework 7 challenge - Koch snowflake
body:
Goal: draw a famous fractal: the Koch snowflake.

A Koch line of depth 0 is a straight line. A Koch line of depth 1 is four lines, each a third as long, with a bump in the middle: ___/\___. Depth 2 does the same thing to each of those four lines, and so on.

  1. Open starter.py and press Run: three triangles appear.
  2. In koch(), replace the straight line in the recursive case with four smaller Koch lines and the turns 60, 120, 60 (follow the TODO).
  3. Run again. The triangles should become snowflakes.

Done looks like: depth 1 = 4 lines per side, depth 2 = 16, depth 3 = 64.

Extra: what happens if you turn left(120) instead of right(120) in snowflake()? Try depth 4 (it has 768 lines!).

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Look at the TODO inside koch(). The straight t.forward(length) at the bottom draws only one plain line. That is why you see triangles. The TODO lists the pieces that should replace it.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: Delete the straight line and write out the list from the TODO, one line at a time. Drawing a smaller Koch line means calling koch again with a shorter length and a depth one smaller. Turning uses t.left(...) and t.right(...).

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: You need four smaller Koch lines, each a fraction of the length and one level shallower. Put a turn between each pair of lines. Read the TODO to see which way to turn and by how many degrees. Keep the early return in the base case so the drawing stops.

starter.name: starter.py
starter.raw:
# Koch snowflake (homework challenge)
# A Koch line of depth 0 is a straight line.
# A Koch line of depth n is FOUR Koch lines of depth n-1, each a third as long,
# with a bump in the middle:   ___/\___
# Three Koch lines in a triangle make a snowflake.

import turtle

PALETTE = ["#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#F0E442",
           "#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#CC79A7", "#000000"]


def koch(t, length, depth):
    """Draw one Koch line."""
    if depth == 0:                 # base case: just a straight line
        t.forward(length)
        return
    # TODO: the recursive case. Instead of one straight line, draw
    #   koch(t, length / 3, depth - 1)
    #   turn left 60
    #   koch(t, length / 3, depth - 1)
    #   turn right 120
    #   koch(t, length / 3, depth - 1)
    #   turn left 60
    #   koch(t, length / 3, depth - 1)
    t.forward(length)


def snowflake(t, length, depth):
    """Three Koch lines, turning 120 degrees after each, make a snowflake."""
    for _ in range(3):
        koch(t, length, depth)
        t.right(120)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    screen = turtle.Screen()
    screen.title("Koch snowflakes")
    screen.tracer(0)
    t = turtle.Turtle()
    t.hideturtle()
    for depth, x in [(0, -300), (1, -100), (3, 100)]:
        t.penup()
        t.goto(x, 60)
        t.setheading(0)
        t.pendown()
        t.pencolor(PALETTE[depth + 4])
        t.pensize(2)
        snowflake(t, 160, depth)
        t.penup()
        t.goto(x + 80, -170)
        t.pencolor("black")
        t.write(f"depth {depth}", align="center", font=("Arial", 14, "normal"))
    screen.update()
    turtle.done()
